handoff_instructions.required_first_response: After receiving this file, ask the project owner which recorded chat and role they want you to continue as before doing project work.
handoff_instructions.required_question: Which chat and role from this handoff would you like me to continue as?
usage: Use chats as role- and conversation-specific context.
Do not merge unresolved proposals into confirmed architecture.
Treat repository_snapshot as an inventory of main at generation time, not as a substitute for checking current GitHub state.
If a requested chat is not represented here, say so rather than inventing history.

project_level.project_summary: A Godot 4 procedural voxel terrain engine that began as an editor-oriented sampled point-field visualizer and evolved into a modular offline generation and runtime streaming architecture. The project established PointFieldResource as the authoritative regular-lattice scalar-field representation, separated visualization from field ownership, implemented Surface Nets as an algorithm consumer, generated ArrayMesh output, introduced chunk assets and manifests, and then added runtime chunk streaming and target-relative residency. The project also added deterministic headless validation, dedicated validation scenes, browser/mobile QA through GitHub Pages Integration Preview, shared mobile touch controls, version/release workflows, architectural decision records, and a mutable ROADMAP.md. The long-term target is large precomputed terrain such as a several-kilometer asteroid, with generation and meshing remaining offline while runtime becomes primarily an asset loading, residency, and eventual LOD problem.
key_steps: Built PointFieldVisualizer for regular 3D sample lattices, density visualization, FastNoiseLite-driven generation, resource save/load, and editor regeneration.
Moved scalar-field geometry, sample positions, densities, indexing, sampling, validation, serialization state, cell helpers, and generation responsibility into PointFieldResource.
Hardened PointFieldResource as the single source of truth and kept consumers from duplicating field state.
Implemented SurfaceNetsMesher as a field-to-mesh consumer and validated winding/orientation and field freshness contracts.
Established ArrayMesh rendering/display helpers while preserving the mesher boundary.
Designed and implemented chunk-domain types including TerrainChunk, TerrainChunkAsset, TerrainChunkManifestEntry, TerrainChunkManifest, and ChunkAssetBaker.
Implemented ChunkStreamer for precomputed runtime chunk loading/unloading and later target-relative residency behavior.
Added chunk validation and chunk streaming validation scenes with headless coverage.
Added a long-lived GitHub Pages Integration Preview and preserved immutable release demos.
Added shared MobileTouchControls for browser/mobile validation.
Added release/version validation workflows, web-demo manifest tooling, and architectural/roadmap documentation.
Adopted architectural decision records and a mutable ROADMAP.md for humans and agents to use as planning inputs.
Shifted roadmap priority toward resource loading and runtime asset residency before LOD.

ownership_rules: PointFieldResource is the authoritative sampled scalar-field representation and remains algorithm-independent.
PointFieldVisualizer and other visualization types are consumers, not field authorities.
SurfaceNetsMesher is a field-to-mesh consumer and must not own noise, chunk streaming, scene-tree state, or field configuration.
TerrainChunkAsset and TerrainChunkManifest describe persisted chunk data and lookup metadata, not runtime generation policy.
ChunkStreamer owns runtime chunk loading/residency and must consume precomputed assets rather than invoke field generation or Surface Nets.
Do not weaken engine contracts merely to optimize or make demos easier.

project_owner_expectations: Act as a senior engine programmer and co-designer, not merely as a code generator.
Consider architecture and long-term maintainability when proposing or implementing features.
Explain significant design decisions and tradeoffs.
Identify unnecessary coupling, duplicated responsibilities, and unclear ownership.
Keep future Surface Nets, Dual Contouring, chunked terrain, and likely extensions in mind without over-engineering.
Favor reusable, well-defined APIs when the additional complexity is justified.
Suggest refactors only when they materially improve maintainability, correctness, performance, or extensibility.
Complete focused implementation/fix requests first unless an architectural problem would make the implementation incorrect or create significant technical debt.
Name branches after the feature being worked on, never generic names.
Every substantial engine feature requires a dedicated validation scene, relevant headless validation, and GitHub Pages Integration Preview exposure when browser-suitable.
Integration Preview categories are long-lived subsystem validation surfaces; extend the existing category in place when practical.
For runtime streaming features, update the existing streaming Integration Preview at preview/integration/streaming/.
Planning and architecture documents are used by both humans and agents; they should describe decisions, constraints, and outcomes without prescribing implementation to competent professionals.

chats.title: Procedural Terrain Architecture
chats.role: Senior engine architect / engineering mentor reviewing architecture, roadmap, planning quality, and agent work.
chats.summary: Reviewed prior chat work as a mentor, assessed engineering behavior, created improvement guidance, repeatedly analyzed updated main, established ADR/roadmap recording, and reviewed planning proposals including resource-loading analysis. The chat became the primary architecture-governance thread.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects architecture-aware mentorship, practical recommendations, firm but constructive review, and architecture/roadmap documents useful to humans and agents without prescribing implementation to competent professionals.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: Record architectural decisions and roadmap adjustments derived from analyses of updated main.
Keep ROADMAP.md mutable and update it alongside architecture records.
Planning artifacts should define context, constraints, decisions, and desired outcomes rather than implementation recipes.
Resource loading was elevated ahead of LOD in the roadmap.

chats.title: Godot Voxel Terrain Progress
chats.role: Senior Godot 4 engine programmer validating milestone completion and deployment status.
chats.summary: Tracked the completed foundational generation and first runtime streaming architecture, especially chunk residency PR #43 and its validation/demo requirements. The chat was used to confirm green CI and website publication.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects repository state, CI, and published demo claims to be verified rather than assumed, while preserving the project's architecture and validation conventions.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: Runtime residency is target-relative and manifest-driven.
Streaming validation must use the existing /streaming/ Integration Preview rather than inventing a feature-specific category.

chats.title: Chunk Residency Implementation
chats.role: Senior Godot 4 engine programmer implementing target-relative chunk residency and validation.
chats.summary: Extended ChunkStreamer from individual load/unload operations into deterministic target-relative residency. The owner corrected the work when validation coverage and web exposure were incomplete, reinforcing that substantial features are not done until the dedicated validation scene, headless tests, and relevant Integration Preview behavior exist.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner is strict that validation must exercise real runtime paths, fail clearly, and update the existing streaming Integration Preview in place.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: A substantial runtime feature must include a validation test scene.
Validation scenes intended for human QA must be exposed through GitHub Pages.
For streaming features, update the existing streaming Integration Preview in place.
A realistic terrain chunk generated from noise is appropriate validation data when it exercises the production path.

chats.title: API Assessment Review
chats.role: Senior Godot 4 engine programmer preparing nf/integration for merge and hardening browser validation.
chats.summary: Reviewed three demos, added ChunkStreamingValidationDemo to the web deployment path, fixed missing demo data, switched streaming validation to real noise-generated chunk content, and prepared the integration PR after architecture/tests/browser QA were satisfactory. Version bump work was needed to restore green checks.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects integration work to be green, browser-testable, architecture-correct, and versioned consistently before merge.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: Streaming demo must be exported and present in the shared demo selector.
Validation should use real production-path terrain data rather than a hollow mock when practical.
Versioning/check requirements are part of PR readiness.

chats.title: API Review and Refinement
chats.role: Senior Godot 4 engine programmer auditing and finishing PointFieldResource API contracts.
chats.summary: Focused on the scalar-field API after the architecture had matured. The chat emphasized field freshness, authoritative indexing, bulk density installation, consumer correctness, documentation conventions, and avoiding unnecessary wrappers or broad refactors.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects a stable algorithm-independent field contract, small justified API changes, and no redesign merely for elegance.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: PointFieldResource remains the algorithm-independent scalar-field authority.
Cell indexing belongs on PointFieldResource rather than being duplicated in SurfaceNetsMesher.
Consumers should require current field data, not merely correctly sized arrays.
Bulk density installation is preferable to exposing dirty-state manipulation.
Do not add redundant xyz wrapper methods when Vector3i APIs already express the contract.

chats.title: Add a player control UI for touch on mobile
chats.role: Senior Godot 4 gameplay/tooling programmer adding mobile browser controls for validation demos.
chats.summary: Added and iterated touch controls so browser/mobile demos can be navigated and validated. Work later converged on a shared MobileTouchControls implementation used by multiple demos.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects mobile controls to serve real human QA without duplicating production or demo logic unnecessarily.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: Use one shared touch-control implementation rather than duplicating demo-specific mobile controllers.
Web-specific touch detection fallbacks should remain isolated from native input behavior.

chats.title: Dual Contouring Explanation
chats.role: Computer science professor and videogame programmer specializing in voxel terrain and meshing systems.
chats.summary: Explained Dual Contouring from scalar-field sign changes through Hermite samples, gradients, tangent-plane constraints, QEF minimization, topology generation, and chunk-boundary concerns, tied to the existing PointFieldResource/Surface Nets architecture.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner wanted a conceptual and implementation-oriented explanation detailed enough to develop Dual Contouring later, while preserving current architecture and avoiding premature abstractions.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: Dual Contouring should be a separate mesher consuming PointFieldResource.
A future QEF solver should be a math utility with no terrain-engine ownership.
Shared Surface Nets/Dual Contouring abstractions should emerge from concrete duplication rather than premature framework design.
Sample-space and cell-space coordinate domains should remain explicit.

chats.title: Chunking System Design
chats.role: Senior engine architect co-designing chunked terrain generation and runtime boundaries.
chats.summary: Designed the conceptual transition from a single scalar field and mesh into deterministic Vector3i-addressed generation chunks, persisted chunk assets/manifests, and runtime streaming. The discussion established the offline/runtime split that later became production architecture.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects chunking to scale the system without contaminating PointFieldResource or mesher responsibilities with streaming concerns.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: PointFieldResource should remain chunk-local-capable without becoming streaming-aware.
Chunk identity should use deterministic Vector3i coordinates.
Boundary sample ownership must support seam-free neighboring meshes.
Runtime should stream precomputed chunk assets rather than generate terrain.

chats.title: Surface Net Mesher Design
chats.role: Senior graphics/engine programmer designing and implementing Surface Nets.
chats.summary: Designed and implemented SurfaceNetsMesher consuming PointFieldResource, then kept the branch updated with main, repaired failing checks, handled semantic versioning for the major feature, and reviewed the feature branch's implemented scope.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects the mesher to be readable, correct, stateless with respect to field ownership, and compatible with future Dual Contouring without generic-framework overreach.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: Surface Nets is a stateless consumer of PointFieldResource.
Version 0.2.0 was considered appropriate for the first major Surface Nets feature milestone under the then-current convention.
Branch work should stay feature-named.

chats.title: Voxel Terrain Generator GDScript
chats.role: Senior Godot 4 engine programmer evolving the initial editor voxel-field prototype into a clean resource/visualizer architecture.
chats.summary: Built the original point-field tooling: field-size editing, resource save/load, density generation toggles, density visualization, FastNoiseLite change watching, and ownership analysis. This chat produced the first detailed split between PointFieldResource and PointFieldVisualizer and seeded the later architecture.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects practical Godot implementation plus architectural guidance, modular editor-friendly design, official GDScript style, public ## docs, stable class_name PointFieldVisualizer, and string-based deferred calls.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: PointFieldResource should own geometry, positions, densities, indexing, sampling, serialization, and generation state.
PointFieldVisualizer should remain visualization-only.
Use string names for deferred calls.
Keep class_name PointFieldVisualizer.
Split regeneration by responsibility rather than one giant update.
All work branches should be named after the feature.

chats.title: Workflows
chats.role: Senior CI/CD and Godot web-deployment engineer maintaining GitHub Actions and GitHub Pages demos.
chats.summary: Debugged invalid workflow expressions, Node runtime deprecation warnings, failed web export/archive steps, and the evolving deployment model. The thread helped establish immutable release demos plus a mutable Integration Preview with manifest/selector injection.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects deployment failures to be investigated to green, existing URLs preserved, and workflow changes kept understandable and maintainable.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: Preserve existing demo URLs and immutable release behavior.
Integration Preview is mutable and intended for current human QA.
Shared demo-selector injection and a generated manifest are the standard publication path.

chats.title: New splash screen design
chats.role: Visual/product designer plus implementation partner for project branding.
chats.summary: Iterated the project splash from a more elaborate Nova Field/tree concept to a simpler title-centered design, integrated the final asset into the repository, and adjusted it through a PR. A small Godot icon was later requested at bottom right.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner prefers restrained project identity and simple graphic hierarchy rather than decorative clutter.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: Keep the splash simple and project-focused.
Use SVG as source artwork and a PNG runtime artifact when needed by Godot/runtime behavior.

chats.title: Connecting GitHub to Project
chats.role: Repository setup and project documentation assistant.
chats.summary: Helped connect the project to GitHub, draft repository descriptions at multiple lengths, discuss private-repository access through the GitHub connector, and establish the repository as the shared implementation surface.
chats.relationship_with_project_owner: The owner expects the assistant to use the connected GitHub repository directly when appropriate and distinguish connector capability from generic web access.
key_decisions_or_outcomes: GitHub connector access is the preferred path for repository state and changes.
